issues.description: nevra[0].lower() uses first character of filename, which may include a directory prefix that breaks koji path layout
issues.detail: The line `nevra = url.split('/')[-1]` extracts the final path component (the .rpm filename). Then `nevra[0].lower()` takes the first character to build the koji subdirectory (canonical koji layout: /Packages/<first-letter-of-name>/<NEVRA>). This works for typical package names but is fragile: if any URL ends with anything other than a package filename starting with a name character (e.g. a digit-prefixed package like '389-ds-base'), the subdirectory will be a digit, which is actually valid in koji layout but the comment 'nevra[0].lower()' should ideally use the package NAME's first letter, not NEVRA. NEVRA filenames always start with the package name's first character so this happens to be correct — but the variable is misnamed (it is a filename, not a NEVRA string in the strict N-E:V-R.A sense). More critically, lower() is unnecessary/incorrect: koji's canonical path uses the literal first character of the package name preserving case-insensitivity by convention but typically the first char is already lowercase for Fedora packages; for packages starting with uppercase (e.g. 'ImageMagick'), forcing lowercase will produce a wrong path that 404s.

issues.description: extract_arch_from_url can return None, leading to a malformed URL with the literal string 'None'
issues.detail: If `extract_arch_from_url` fails to match any of the four arches, it returns None. The caller then does `koji_url_base + f'/latest/{arch}/Packages'`, producing a URL containing '/latest/None/Packages/...'. This is silently appended to `updated_list` and will fail later when Konflux/hermeto tries to fetch it. The function should raise an exception or the caller should validate and abort with a clear error so the failure mode is loud, not a 404 deep in the build pipeline.

issues.description: Arch detection by regex search may match the wrong arch when the URL contains multiple arch tokens
issues.detail: `extract_arch_from_url` does a regex `search` and returns the first match. URLs like '.../releases/40/Everything/x86_64/os/Packages/.../foo.ppc64le.rpm' contain two arch tokens (path component and rpm suffix). The first match wins, which may be the repo-path arch rather than the package arch. For Fedora secondary arches in particular, the path might be '/pub/fedora-secondary/.../ppc64le/...' which is correct, but cross-arch resolution edge cases (noarch packages, mixed paths) should be handled by parsing the .rpm filename suffix directly (the `.{arch}.rpm` is unambiguous) rather than scanning the whole URL.

issues.description: noarch packages are not handled — they have no arch token in their filename suffix
issues.detail: Noarch RPMs end in `.noarch.rpm`, but 'noarch' is not in the arches list. If a URL points to a noarch package and the URL path also lacks an x86_64/aarch64/ppc64le/s390x token (unlikely but possible for some repo layouts), the function returns None. Even if the URL path contains an arch token, the constructed koji URL would route the noarch package into an arch-specific Packages directory, which may or may not be correct depending on koji's layout for coreos-pool. The PR should explicitly decide: do noarch packages live under each arch's Packages dir in coreos-pool, or under a separate noarch tree? Verify against an actual coreos-pool listing.

issues.description: Race condition between bump-lockfile merge and coreos-koji-tagger acknowledged but not mitigated
issues.detail: The PR description openly states there is a possible race condition between the koji tag operation and CI/CD hermetic builds, and that rpms.lock.yaml changes cannot be tested locally. There is no retry, no verification step, no warning logged when the constructed URL points to a not-yet-tagged build, and no documentation in the script itself about this constraint. Operators debugging a failed Konflux build will have no breadcrumb pointing at this race. At minimum, add a comment in the code referencing the bump-lockfile/koji-tagger dependency and consider a HEAD probe with a clear error message when the constructed URL 404s.

issues.description: Dead/legacy code: the coreos-pool prioritization in query_packages_location is now redundant
issues.detail: After this change, every URL is rewritten in `use_koji_url_only` to a coreos-pool URL regardless of what `query_packages_location` returned. The prioritization logic in `query_packages_location` (lines around 158-162, the `if 'coreos-pool' in url or not existing_url` branch) is now mostly defensive dead weight — its output is always overwritten. Either remove the prioritization (since rewriting makes it moot) or keep it and document why both layers exist. Keeping silent redundant logic invites future confusion.

issues.description: Hard-coded koji URL base with no override hook
issues.detail: `koji_url_base = 'https://kojipkgs.fedoraproject.org/repos-dist/coreos-pool'` is a magic string buried in a function. If Fedora ever migrates the path (they have done so historically), or if a downstream/derived project wants to use a different koji instance, this requires a code edit. Lift to a module-level constant at minimum, ideally make it overridable via env var or CLI arg consistent with how the rest of the script is parameterized.

issues.description: Variable named `nevra` actually holds an RPM filename, not a NEVRA string
issues.detail: A NEVRA is 'name-epoch:version-release.arch'. The variable holds 'name-version-release.arch.rpm' (the filename with .rpm suffix, no epoch). Minor naming nit but matters for readers trying to understand what is being passed to koji's path layout.

issues.description: No unit tests added for new URL rewriting logic
issues.detail: `use_koji_url_only` and `extract_arch_from_url` are pure functions that are trivially unit-testable. Given the PR explicitly notes that changes cannot be tested locally end-to-end, unit tests around the URL rewriting are the only realistic safety net. A handful of table-driven cases (coreos-pool URL passthrough, fedora secondary arch rewrite, ImageMagick-style capitalized name, noarch, missing arch) would catch most P0/P1 issues above.

issues.description: Substring match `koji_url_base in url` is loose
issues.detail: Using `in` for URL identification will also match URLs that contain the coreos-pool base as a substring in an unexpected position (unlikely in practice, but `url.startswith(koji_url_base)` is the more precise check). Also, this comparison would fail if Fedora ever serves the same content via `https://kojipkgs.fedoraproject.org/repos/coreos-pool` (no '-dist'), even though semantically those are the same artifact. Consider parsing the URL and checking host+path-prefix.

issues.description: PR header says 'Language: Go' but the file is Python
issues.detail: Informational only — the PR metadata is wrong. The script is Python (uses `import`, `yaml`, `re`, `subprocess`). Worth noting because reviewers shouldn't expect Go idioms here. Does not affect correctness.

dissents.topic: How loudly should missing arch / unknown URL formats fail?

positions.position: Return None and let the downstream fetch fail with a 404. The script is internal to coreos-assembler CI, errors will surface eventually, and adding strict validation now is premature.

Silent None-to-string coercion that produces a literal '/None/' in a URL is the worst failure mode: looks valid, fails far from cause. Raise immediately in extract_arch_from_url or assert in use_koji_url_only.

dissents.topic: Is the acknowledged race condition acceptable?

positions.position: PR description states it's only consumed by Konflux today, and the koji-tagger runs on merge. The race window is small, and a failed Konflux build is recoverable. Ship it.

Writing URLs to a lockfile that may not resolve yet violates the lockfile's invariant (lockfiles point to artifacts that exist). At minimum, add a HEAD-probe verification step or a documented retry policy so a future operator isn't blindsided.

dissents.topic: Should the coreos-pool prioritization in query_packages_location be removed?

positions.position: The downstream rewrite makes the upstream prioritization moot. Remove it to reduce surface area and avoid two layers of 'special handling' for the same problem.
Keep it. If use_koji_url_only is ever bypassed or refactored, the prioritization still does something useful. Cost of keeping it is low.

dissents.topic: Arch detection: regex on full URL vs filename-suffix parsing

positions.position: The regex with word boundaries is fine. Fedora repo URLs always contain the arch in a path component, and the first hit will be correct in practice for the input space we care about.

Parse the .rpm filename suffix (`name-version-release.ARCH.rpm`). It's unambiguous, locally defined, and doesn't depend on the shape of upstream repo paths. The regex search is incidentally correct, not structurally correct.

review.summary: The PR replaces a DNF5 workaround (prioritizing coreos-pool URLs in repoquery output) with a more aggressive approach: rewrite every package URL into the canonical koji coreos-pool path. The core idea is sound and the diff is small, but the implementation has two real correctness risks: (1) `nevra[0].lower()` forces the package-name first letter to lowercase, which will produce wrong paths for capitalized packages like `ImageMagick`, and (2) `extract_arch_from_url` can return `None`, silently producing a URL with a literal `'None'` segment. Both should be fixed before merge. Additionally, the acknowledged race with coreos-koji-tagger and the inability to test locally argue strongly for adding unit tests around the new pure functions, even though end-to-end testing is gated on Konflux. Lower-priority cleanups: the now-redundant coreos-pool prioritization in `query_packages_location`, the hard-coded URL base, and a misleading variable name. PR header lists Go as the language but the file is Python.
